_note: Text for the code step of build mode (issue #58), in ASD-STE100. lib/sketch fills in {line}, {name}, {sign}, {found}, {want}, {pin}, {what}, {suggest}, {led}, {on}, {off}, {want_on} and {want_off}. Each error starts with "Line {line}: ", so the learner knows which line to fix. Use short words: the learner may never have seen code.

errors.unknown_sign: Jumper does not know the sign {sign}. Check this line for a typing mistake.
errors.unsupported_sign: Jumper does not use the sign {sign} yet. To compare two values, use == or !=.
errors.unsupported_text: Jumper does not use text in quotes yet. Remove the quotes and the text between them.
errors.unsupported_word: Jumper does not run {name} yet. You can use int, const int, pinMode, digitalWrite, digitalRead, delay, if and else.
errors.own_function: Jumper does not run functions that you make yet. Use only setup() and loop().
errors.unknown_function: Jumper does not know the function {name}. You can use pinMode, digitalWrite, digitalRead and delay.
errors.missing_semicolon: Put a ; at the end of this line.
errors.missing_close_brace: This { has no }. Each { needs a } to close it.
errors.extra_brace: This } has no { before it. Remove it.
errors.bad_value: Jumper needs a value here, for example 13, HIGH, LOW or the name of a variable. It found {found}.
errors.unknown_name: Jumper does not know {name}. Check the spelling. If it is a variable, make it first, for example: int {name} = 0;
errors.unknown_name_case: Jumper does not know {name}. Did you mean {suggest}? Big and small letters must be the same.
errors.bad_mode: The mode of pinMode must be INPUT, OUTPUT or INPUT_PULLUP.
errors.not_a_value: {name} does not give a value. Put it on its own line.
errors.use_double_equals: Use == to compare two values. One = puts a value into a variable.
errors.const_change: {name} is a const int, so you cannot change it.
errors.fixed_name: You cannot change {name}. It is a fixed name of the Arduino.
errors.redeclare: {name} is already made. Make each variable only one time.
errors.const_needs_value: A const int needs a value, for example: const int {name} = 13;
errors.outside_function: This line is outside setup() and loop(). Put it inside the { } of setup() or loop().
errors.duplicate_function: There are two {name}() functions. Keep only one.
errors.no_setup: Your sketch needs void setup() { }. It runs one time, at the start.
errors.no_loop: Your sketch needs void loop() { }. It runs again and again, after setup().
errors.bad_pin: The Uno has no pin {pin}. Use a pin from 0 to 13.
errors.no_delay: loop() runs again and again with no pause, so Jumper stopped the sketch. Add delay(10); at the end of loop().

functions.pinMode: two values: the pin and the mode
functions.digitalWrite: two values: the pin and HIGH or LOW
functions.delay: one value: the time in milliseconds

want.name: a name
want.function: a function name, setup or loop

notes.write_not_output: Line {line}: Pin {pin} is not an OUTPUT, so it cannot light the LED. Add pinMode({pin}, OUTPUT); to setup().
notes.read_floating: Line {line}: Pin {pin} is an INPUT with no pull-up resistor, so it reads LOW even when nobody presses the button. Use INPUT_PULLUP in pinMode.

goal.stays_off: {led} stays off. It must turn on for {want_on} ms.
goal.stays_on: {led} stays on. It must turn off for {want_off} ms.
goal.timing: {led} is on for {on} ms and off for {off} ms. It must be on for {want_on} ms and off for {want_off} ms.
goal.button_off: {led} stays off when you press the button. It must turn on while you press it.
goal.button_on: {led} stays on when nobody presses the button. It must turn off when you let go.
goal.button_inverted: {led} does the opposite: it is on when nobody presses the button, and off when you press it. Swap HIGH and LOW.
goal.button_unsteady: {led} does not follow the button each time. It must be on while you press the button, and off when you let go.
